simple_definition: The older, cheaper way of connecting a chip to its package: tiny gold or copper wires are stitched from pads on the chip's edge to the package leads.
technical_definition: Interconnect method in which fine Au/Cu/Ag wires connect die bond pads to a leadframe or substrate; the basis of most 'conventional' or 'mainstream' packages (e.g. QFN, SOIC). Amkor classes wirebond packaging as 'mainstream products'.

simple_definition: A way of attaching a chip upside down so that small solder bumps across its whole face connect directly to the package, giving more and shorter connections than wires.
technical_definition: Interconnect in which bumped die are flipped and joined face-down to a substrate (FC-CSP for small packages, FC-BGA for large ones on ABF substrates). Yole and Amkor count flip chip as advanced packaging.

simple_definition: Packaging the chips while they are still on the wafer, so the finished package is barely bigger than the chip itself.
technical_definition: Packaging operations (redistribution layers, bumps) done at wafer level before dicing; fan-in WLCSP keeps I/O within the die footprint. Fan-in WLP was 48% of Yole's 2020 advanced-packaging wafer count.

simple_definition: A wafer-level package where the chip is embedded in a larger moulded area so wiring can spread out beyond the chip's edges, allowing more connections without a traditional substrate.
technical_definition: Die are reconstituted in mould compound on a wafer (FO-WLP) or panel (FO-PLP) and redistribution layers route I/O outside the die footprint (e.g. TSMC InFO).

simple_definition: Putting tiny solder or copper balls on the surface of a wafer so its chips can later be connected face-down to a package.
technical_definition: Wafer-level deposition of solder or Cu-pillar bumps (with under-bump metallisation) required for flip-chip and many wafer-level packages; the SEMI/TechSearch database counted 85-plus bumping facilities in 2024.

simple_definition: The older, labour-heavy, low-margin ways of packaging chips (mostly wire-bonded chips in plastic packages on metal frames), as opposed to advanced packaging.
technical_definition: Non-advanced ATP: leadframe and laminate wire-bond packages (QFN, QFP, SOIC, TSOP, wire-bond BGA) and discrete/power packages. SIA/BCG sized it at US$51bn of a US$95bn ATP market (2024 report). The boundary with 'advanced' differs by publisher.

simple_definition: A small, flat, cheap chip package with metal contacts on its underside edges instead of legs.
technical_definition: Leadframe-based, wire-bonded, moulded package with exposed pads on the bottom perimeter; widely used for analog, power and automotive chips. 100-plus facilities offered QFN per the 2024 SEMI/TechSearch database.

simple_definition: Packaging and testing that a chip company does in its own factories rather than paying a contractor.
technical_definition: Assembly, test and packaging performed by IDMs (Intel, Micron, TI, Infineon) and foundries (TSMC) for their own or their wafer customers' products; valued by CSET at US$25bn in 2019 vs US$28bn OSAT.

simple_definition: The share of all finished wafers that go to advanced packaging versus conventional packaging.
technical_definition: Yole metric: 300mm-equivalent wafers entering advanced vs conventional packaging (19%/81% in 2014; 35%/65% expected by 2026).
